widgets_values: Photorealistic 3D architectural visualization of a Japandi residential house interior, shown from a high bird’s-eye view as an orthographic cutaway floor plan with the roof removed. The wide composition presents the entire single-story home and its distinct functional zones within one continuous plan, surrounded by pale sand-colored ground and sparse native grasses. Warm sunset light enters from the upper right, casting long, soft-edged shadows across warm wood floors, bamboo screens, linen upholstery, and muted earthy surfaces. At the top center, clean dark-brown sans-serif lettering reads "JAPANDI RESIDENCE". The open-plan layout is divided by low timber partitions and sliding shoji-style screens into clearly legible rooms labeled "ENTRY", "LIVING", "DINING", "KITCHEN", "STUDY", "BEDROOMS", "BATH", and "TERRACE". In the lower left, the entry hall contains a woven rush mat, a cedar console table, two ceramic vessels, and a recessed coat niche. Beside it, the living room holds a low oatmeal-colored sofa facing a rectangular walnut coffee table on a natural jute rug, with two rounded lounge chairs, a bamboo pendant lamp, linen curtains, and a sculptural branch arrangement in a clay vase. The dining area occupies the center-left, furnished with a long oval oak table, eight simple spindle-back chairs, and a shallow stone bowl beneath a circular paper lantern. Along the upper center, the kitchen has matte limewashed walls, pale veined marble counters, flat-front oak cabinetry, open shelves with neutral ceramics, a broad island with three stools, and a compact sink beneath a window. On the right, the study contains a built-in desk, reading chair, shelving, and stacked books. Two bedrooms sit along the lower right, each furnished with a low platform bed, rumpled beige bedding, timber headboards, bedside tables, and woven rugs; between them, the bathroom combines pale limestone flooring, a freestanding oval tub, a floating oak vanity, folded towels, and a bamboo shower screen. Wide sliding doors connect the central rooms to a covered terrace lined with timber posts, bamboo fencing, potted olive trees, and a rectangular reflecting pool. Thin dimension lines, wall thicknesses, door swings, stairs, and furniture remain crisp and readable throughout the plan, while the empty rooms contain no people.
